To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of methoxyacetoxy esters and amides significantly enhances reaction rates for the lipase-cata-lyzed preparation of enantio-pure 1-(p-chloro-phenyl) ethyl amides and amines.
the use of methoxy acetates significantly enhances the reaction rate in the lipase-mediated preparation of enantiomerically pure 1-(4- chlorophenyl) ethylamines.

the use of methoxy acetate derivatives as leaving group or as ethyl group in lipase-catalysed reactions of (R,S)-1-(4-chlrophenyl)-ethyl amide significantly enhances reaction rates and that immobilized lipase (from Candida antarctic) is the best biocatalyst for these reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and optimization of a lipase-catalysed process for the preparation of enantiomeric pure 1-(4- chlorophenyl) ethyl amine, a key intermediate in the synthesis of the antidepressant drug milnacipran.
the use of lipase-catalysis in the synthesis of enantiopures (S)-1-(4-chiorphenyl) ethyl amine and (S)-1,2-diphenyl ethyl amine.
the lipase-cata-lyzed preparation of enantioenriched amines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of methoxyacetoxy esters as acyl donor in acylation reactions or as leaving group in hydrolysis reactions of amides significantly enhances reaction rates and results in higher optical purities.
the lipase-caterlyzed hydrolysis of (R,S)-amides is a very useful method for the preparation of enantiomerically pure amines.
the use of methoxyacetoxy esters as ethyl esters in acylation reactions of amines and as leaving groups in the hydrolytic cleavage of amides results in significantly enhanced reaction rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methoxy acetoxygenic group is an excellent leaving group in the lipase catalyzed hydrolysis of amides.
lipase-catalysed hydrolysis or acylation of the two different (R)- or (S)-[1-(p-chlorophenylethyl) amides] gave enantiopure products (99% ee) with high conversion (∼50%) in phosphate buffer.

the lipase-cata-lyzed hydrolysis or acylation of 4-chlorophenyethyl amides and amines is a viable method for preparation of enantiomerically enriched amines, but that the use of methoxyacetoxy esters as leaving groups or acylating agents enhances the reaction rates significantly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
